name: AZ-09
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Paul Gosar running with cash advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~4%
No polls or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The district's R+15 lean, Gosar's incumbency and fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Democratic win at only about 4% all point to a safe Republican hold. No polls or ratings justify moving from the fundamentals-based forecast.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the challenger competitive, or a major scandal or independent spending surge against Gosar, would be the main reason to revisit this.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Paul Gosar seeks another term in a northeastern Arizona district that leans Republican by about fifteen points. He enters the general election with a large cash advantage over Democrat Dani Sterbinsky, who has raised modestly and has little money on hand, and no significant outside spending has materialized on either side. Prediction markets give Gosar roughly a 94% chance of winning.

With no public polls or expert ratings of the race, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and market pricing. The environment favors Republicans this cycle, and nothing in the available evidence suggests the challenger has a realistic path to an upset.
